decisions.content: The 23 skills under skills/ with their references and the two build_ledger.py scripts, and TELEMETRY.md and scripts/doctor.py for the setup.
decisions.reason: Each skill is a procedure for one kind of request (an analysis, a plan, a text, an image, a video), useful only in the task that asks for it and loaded then. None gives rules that hold in every session. One capability per skill: no two produce the same thing. The originals travel whole and each body opens them for the part a task needs. TELEMETRY.md is carried by media-setup, on demand: it answers a question a user asks rarely, and the source itself states it only in that file.

decisions.content: The MCP server the skills call: scripts/supercmo_skills (started by the source as supercmo-skills) with scripts/supercmo_env.py and the two Inter fonts its caption tool uses.
decisions.reason: Breadth and timing: the skills do their work only through this server's tools, so a plugin without it would hand the user an install step before any task; the owner asked that the server be absorbed (2026-11-21). It starts from the packaged files at the pinned release, on the standard library; the source's own registration downloads the published package with uvx. Cost in every session: 22 tools whose descriptions and schemas are 46 KB, about 11,500 tokens where a host loads every schema at start (the packaged server's own tools/list, read on 2026-11-21; a host that defers tool schemas pays less). The package pays it because every capability but three calls these tools. It also registers tools no skill calls (caption_video, video_overlay, transcribe, four calendar tools): they come with the server as shipped. What the tools send, and to which provider, is stated in each capability; the server's own opt-out telemetry is in media-setup. If the original plugin or a server named supercmo is already configured on the host, every tool is offered twice and on some hosts the user's own entry wins: media-setup says so. Open doubt: on Codex and Hermes the server starts in the plugin's folder and its default output folder lands there; media-setup carries the source's variable for it.

decisions.content: The source's own installation and registration: .mcp.json (uvx supercmo-skills@0.1.27), pyproject.toml, the install sections of README.md, the npm installer, the host manifests and marketplace files.
decisions.reason: Installing the source itself. This plugin carries the skills and registers the absorbed server; the original's installer would add a second copy of both. .mcp.json, pyproject.toml and README.md were read as evidence of how the server starts and what it depends on, and are not packaged. The managed-key login (npx @supercmo/skills login) is not installation: it stays in media-setup as the source's way to deliver the key.

decisions.content: skills/*/evals/eval_cases.json, the source's own evaluation cases.
decisions.reason: Tests of the original skills' triggering. They were read to draw each intent's boundaries and are not packaged; no capability runs them.

decisions.content: data/videos.json (703 prompts with category, technique tags, author and original post) and the sections 'How to use a prompt' and 'Credits' of README.md.
decisions.reason: A library consulted only when someone wants a coded animation or a reference prompt. The file is about 810 KB: it is read through a filter inside the task and never loaded in a session. The credit rule (every prompt belongs to its creator) is carried in the capability and checked there. The MIT license covers the collection, not the prompts; the owner chose to absorb it with credits (2026-11-21).

decisions.content: The rest of README.md: the gallery tables, preview images and links to the curator's site.
decisions.reason: Presentation of the collection and promotion of the curator's site. The same entries are in data/videos.json, which keeps each entry's link. README.md is read at intake only and is not packaged.
